status.documented: a source states it (a claim or a relation record)
status.derived: produced by a recorded rule over recorded claims (KG-R1 use → function, KG-R2 height → band, M29 growth form)
status.candidate: inferred from traits by KG-R4, or a model placeholder — never promoted to documented
status.unknown: no evidence to judge, or a recorded trait contradicts a requirement — listed as a gap, never drawn as a link

verification.verified: at least one live supporting claim or record was verified by a human (open data, survey)
verification.unverified: supporting claims exist but no human has verified them
verification.none: no supporting claim: the link is an inference (KG-R4) or an entity record
verification.entity: read from the plant's entity record (identity_review), not from a sourced claim
verification.literature: a literature statement about a concept (requirement), not about a plant

evidence_check.supported_by_source: the AI reviewer found the statement on the source page
evidence_check.partially_supported: the AI reviewer found part of it, or a different wording / unit / scope
evidence_check.conflicting_evidence: the AI reviewer found the source says otherwise
evidence_check.not_assessed: no AI assessment on record (verified claims were not queued)

unknown_verdict.evidence missing: no claim on a required trait — the database does not know; not a suitability verdict
unknown_verdict.contradicted by traits: a recorded claim places the plant outside a required trait — evidence against, under the stated conditions, cultivar and source

pair_sections.shared_attributes: concepts both plants reach through their own claims — a computable overlap, not companion-planting evidence
pair_sections.direct_relations: records in relations.json for this pair — the only direct plant-to-plant knowledge; retired records are history
pair_sections.spatial_complementarity: distinct spatial functions the two plants' live links allow — a design hypothesis pending site, spacing and biological checks
pair_sections.evidence_unknowns: sources behind the above, and what the database does not know about the pair

groups.label: Environment
groups.definition: Light, soil, water, habitat and hardiness the plant needs or tolerates.

groups.label: Growth & Form
groups.definition: Height band, habit, form, texture and growth rate — how big and what shape the plant becomes.

groups.label: Seasonal & Ecological Performance
groups.definition: Leaf retention, colour, seasonal interest, fruit, wildlife value and origin.

groups.label: Maintenance & Risk
groups.definition: Maintenance level, stress and browsing resistance, pests, diseases and toxicity.

facets.label: Light
facets.definition: Light the site offers, KPU's exposure facet with three groups (sun, part shade, shade).

facets.label: Soil
facets.definition: Soil types a plant takes, KPU's soil facet.

facets.label: Water
facets.definition: Water and drainage regime the plant needs.

facets.label: Habitat class (E-Flora)
facets.definition: Habitat classes a plant is recorded in by E-Flora BC (normalised, M43); a shared class is an indirect connection, not a planting relation.

facets.label: Hardiness (USDA zones)
facets.definition: USDA hardiness zones as given by US sources.

facets.label: Hardiness (RHS ratings)
facets.definition: RHS hardiness ratings H1–H7.

facets.label: BC biogeoclimatic zone
facets.definition: Biogeoclimatic zones (BEC) an E-Flora atlas page lists the plant in; CWH is Metro Vancouver's zone.

facets.label: Height bands
facets.definition: Robinson's five planting-height bands, from carpeting plants to trees.

facets.label: Habit
facets.definition: Branching and growth habit (KPU habit facet).

facets.label: Form
facets.definition: Overall outline of the plant (KPU form facet).

facets.label: Texture
facets.definition: Visual texture, fine to very coarse (KPU).

facets.label: Growth rate
facets.definition: Slow, moderate or fast growth.

facets.label: Height
facets.definition: KPU mature-height classes; quantitative claims span the classes their range covers.

facets.label: Spread
facets.definition: KPU mature-spread classes.

facets.label: Plant age
facets.definition: Age bands of the plant at the time a value holds.

facets.label: Leaf retention
facets.definition: Whether leaves are held through winter.

facets.label: Seasonal interest
facets.definition: Seasonal interest features (fall colour, winter interest).

facets.label: Fruit
facets.definition: Fruit character (edible, showy).

facets.label: Colour
facets.definition: Flower and foliage colours (KPU colour list).

facets.label: Habitat & ecological value
facets.definition: Ecological values a plant offers: native, pollinator, bird food, cover, erosion control, habitat structure.

facets.label: Origin status
facets.definition: Native or non-native status for BC.

facets.label: Invasive status
facets.definition: Invasive-species listing status in BC.

facets.label: Maintenance
facets.definition: Maintenance level required.

facets.label: Stress tolerance
facets.definition: Abiotic stresses tolerated (drought, salt, wind, winter wet…).

facets.label: Browsing resistance
facets.definition: Resistance to deer and rabbit browsing.

facets.label: Pests & diseases
facets.definition: Pests and diseases, as susceptibility or as resistance.

facets.label: Toxicity
facets.definition: Toxicity to pets, humans or livestock.

concepts.label: Deep shade
concepts.definition: Less than about two hours of direct sun; under dense canopy or on the north side of buildings.

concepts.label: Filtered shade
concepts.definition: Light reaching the plant through a tree canopy or lattice all day; bright but never direct for long.

concepts.label: Full sun
concepts.definition: Six or more hours of direct sun in summer; no overhead canopy.

concepts.label: Full sun only if soil kept moist
concepts.definition: Takes full sun only where the soil does not dry out; in dry sun it scorches or stalls.

concepts.label: Part sun/part shade
concepts.definition: Three to six hours of direct sun, or dappled light for much of the day.

concepts.label: Sheltered
concepts.definition: A position protected from strong or cold wind, for example near a wall or inside a planting.

concepts.label: bog
concepts.definition: Peat bogs: wet, acidic, nutrient-poor ground.

concepts.label: coastal
concepts.definition: Shoreline and coastal sites exposed to salt and wind.

concepts.label: disturbed
concepts.definition: Roadsides, cutover and other disturbed ground.

concepts.label: forest
concepts.definition: Under or at the edge of tree canopy, dry to wet forest.

concepts.label: grassland
concepts.definition: Grassland, prairie and steppe; open and usually dry.

concepts.label: meadow
concepts.definition: Open herbaceous ground, moist to dry meadows.

concepts.label: rocky
concepts.definition: Rock outcrops, bluffs, talus and shallow soils.

concepts.label: streamside
concepts.definition: Stream, river and lake margins; riparian ground.

concepts.label: swamp
concepts.definition: Swamps and marshes with standing or slow water.

concepts.label: Acidic
concepts.definition: Soil with pH below about 6.5, typical of coastal BC under conifers.

concepts.label: Alkaline
concepts.definition: Soil with pH above about 7.5, usually over limestone or where lime has been added.

concepts.label: Humus rich
concepts.definition: Dark soil high in decomposed organic matter; holds moisture and nutrients well.

concepts.label: Rocky or gravelly or dry
concepts.definition: Thin, stony or sandy ground that drains fast and holds little water or nutrient.

concepts.label: Well-drained
concepts.definition: Soil through which water passes freely, so roots are never left standing in water.

concepts.label: average
concepts.definition: Ordinary garden moisture: rain plus occasional watering, neither dry nor wet for long.

concepts.label: dry
concepts.definition: Little available soil moisture for long periods; relies on rain or drought tolerance.

concepts.label: moist
concepts.definition: Soil that stays damp but not waterlogged, such as a shaded bed or a slope base.

concepts.label: wet
concepts.definition: Soil often saturated: pond margins, ditches, poorly drained low ground.

concepts.label: wide range
concepts.definition: Tolerates anything from dry to wet once established.

concepts.label: Creeping / Mat-like
concepts.definition: Overall form: Spreads along the ground, staying low.

concepts.label: Mounded
concepts.definition: Overall form: A low, rounded dome wider than tall.

concepts.label: Pyramidal - widely
concepts.definition: Overall form: A broad cone, wide at the base.

concepts.label: Round
concepts.definition: Overall form: About as tall as wide, with a rounded crown.

concepts.label: fast
concepts.definition: Gains height or spread quickly; may need room or restraint early.

concepts.label: moderate
concepts.definition: Reaches mature size in a normal span of years for its type.

concepts.label: slow
concepts.definition: Adds little each year; takes many years to reach its mature size.

concepts.label: Arching
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Branches rise then bend over in arcs.

concepts.label: Dense
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Closely branched with little open space.

concepts.label: Horizontal
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Branches held level, in layers.

concepts.label: Spreading
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Branches extend outward, wider than tall.

concepts.label: Stiffly upright
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Rigid, vertical branches.

concepts.label: Upright
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Grows mainly upward.

concepts.label: Ground-level planting (carpeting)
concepts.definition: Carpeting plants at ground level. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

concepts.label: Low planting (below knee)
concepts.definition: Shrubs and herbaceous plants below knee height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

concepts.label: Medium-height planting (knee to eye level)
concepts.definition: Planting between knee and eye level: a physical barrier that still allows views over it. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

concepts.label: Tall shrub planting (above eye level)
concepts.definition: Planting above eye level: visual enclosure and screening. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

concepts.label: Tree planting
concepts.definition: Trees: canopy, ceiling and shade above head height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

concepts.label: Coarse
concepts.definition: Visual texture 'Coarse': how coarse or fine the leaves and branching read from a distance.

concepts.label: Fine
concepts.definition: Visual texture 'Fine': how coarse or fine the leaves and branching read from a distance.

concepts.label: Medium
concepts.definition: Visual texture 'Medium': how coarse or fine the leaves and branching read from a distance.

concepts.label: deer
concepts.definition: Browsing by deer, a common cause of damage in the North Shore and suburbs.

concepts.label: rabbit
concepts.definition: Browsing by rabbits, mainly on young growth.

concepts.label: low
concepts.definition: Needs little pruning, feeding or clean-up once established.

concepts.label: medium
concepts.definition: Needs some seasonal attention: shaping, feeding or leaf clean-up.

concepts.label: Abiotic disorder
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Abiotic disorder': Damage from non-living causes: weather, soil, chemicals.

concepts.label: Anthracnose
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Anthracnose': A fungal disease causing leaf and shoot blight, worse in wet springs.

concepts.label: Aphids
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Aphids': Small sap-sucking insects that cluster on new growth.

concepts.label: Beetles or weevils
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Beetles or weevils': Chewing beetles; root weevils notch leaves and eat roots.

concepts.label: Blight or needle cast
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Blight or needle cast': Fungal dieback of shoots or shedding of needles.

concepts.label: Canker or sap rot
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Canker or sap rot': Dead sunken bark patches, often oozing.

concepts.label: Caterpillar or cutworm
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Caterpillar or cutworm': Larvae that chew leaves or cut stems.

concepts.label: Crown rot
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Crown rot': Rot at the base of the plant, usually from wet soil.

concepts.label: Fungal leaf spot
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Fungal leaf spot': Spots on leaves caused by fungi.

concepts.label: Galls
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Galls': Abnormal swellings caused by insects or mites.

concepts.label: Leaf miner insect
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf miner insect': Larvae that tunnel inside leaves.

concepts.label: Leaf scorch
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf scorch': Browning of leaf edges from sun, wind or drought.

concepts.label: Mildew
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Mildew': Powdery or downy fungal coating on leaves.

concepts.label: Mites
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Mites': Tiny sap-sucking arachnids causing stippled leaves.

concepts.label: Root rot
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Root rot': Root decay from fungi in wet soil.

concepts.label: Rust
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Rust': Orange fungal pustules on leaves.

concepts.label: Scale insects
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Scale insects': Immobile sap-sucking insects under a waxy shell.

concepts.label: Slugs or snails
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Slugs or snails': Molluscs that chew holes in leaves.

concepts.label: Wilt
concepts.definition: Pest or disease 'Wilt': Vascular disease causing drooping and death of branches.

concepts.label: disease
concepts.definition: Fungal, bacterial and viral diseases in general.

concepts.label: pest
concepts.definition: Insect and mite pests in general.

concepts.label: black walnut
concepts.definition: Juglone, the chemical black walnut roots release, which kills many plants nearby.

concepts.label: clay soil
concepts.definition: Heavy, slow-draining clay, the usual Vancouver subsoil once topsoil is stripped.

concepts.label: drought
concepts.definition: Dry spells without irrigation once established.

concepts.label: erosion
concepts.definition: Unstable or eroding ground on slopes and banks where soil moves.

concepts.label: leaf scorch
concepts.definition: Browning of leaf edges from sun, wind or drought.

concepts.label: salt
concepts.definition: Road salt spray or saline soil.

concepts.label: urban pollution
concepts.definition: Exhaust, dust and compacted soil of streets.

concepts.label: wet soil
concepts.definition: Soil that stays saturated for long periods; rain gardens, swales, low ground.

concepts.label: winter wet
concepts.definition: Saturated soil through the wet season.

concepts.label: Bronze
concepts.definition: Bronze as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Dark-red
concepts.definition: Dark-red as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Green
concepts.definition: Green as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Orange
concepts.definition: Orange as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Pink
concepts.definition: Pink as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Purple
concepts.definition: Purple as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Red
concepts.definition: Red as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: White
concepts.definition: White as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: Yellow
concepts.definition: Yellow as a flower, foliage or fruit colour in the KPU colour list.

concepts.label: bird food
concepts.definition: Fruit or seed eaten by birds.

concepts.label: erosion control
concepts.definition: Roots hold soil on slopes and banks.

concepts.label: pollinator
concepts.definition: Flowers feed bees and other pollinating insects.

concepts.label: wildlife cover
concepts.definition: Dense growth that shelters birds or small animals.

concepts.label: Deciduous
concepts.definition: Drops its leaves in autumn and stands bare in winter.

concepts.label: Evergreen
concepts.definition: Keeps its leaves through winter, so it reads the same all year.

concepts.label: Edible fruit
concepts.definition: Produces fruit people can eat.

concepts.label: Showy fruit
concepts.definition: Produces fruit noticed for its colour or persistence rather than for eating.

concepts.label: Fall colour
concepts.definition: Leaves turn a notable colour in autumn before dropping.

concepts.label: Winter interest
concepts.definition: Something to look at in winter: bark, berries, structure or evergreen leaves.

concepts.label: Not listed as invasive
concepts.definition: Does not appear on BC or ISCBC invasive lists.

concepts.label: Native
concepts.definition: Occurs naturally in the region without having been introduced by people.

concepts.label: Native to BC west of the Cascades
concepts.definition: Grows naturally in coastal BC, the Vancouver region included.

concepts.label: Native to North America
concepts.definition: Native to the continent but not to coastal BC.

concepts.label: Non-native
concepts.definition: Introduced from elsewhere; not naturally occurring here.

concepts.label: Tree
concepts.definition: A woody plant usually with a single trunk, reaching well above head height at maturity.

concepts.label: Open
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Widely spaced branches you can see through.

concepts.label: Twiggy
concepts.definition: Branching habit: Many fine, short branches.

relations.text: A practising designer listed Vaccinium ovatum and Gaultheria shallon together in a five-plant list for Metro Vancouver, both as evergreen natives.
relations.context: survey d1, same respondent list (with Gaillardia aristata, Eriophyllum lanatum, Campanula rotundifolia)
relations.note: co-listing is weak evidence of compatibility — it records that a designer thinks of them together, nothing more

relations.text: Vaccinium ovatum and Gaultheria shallon co-occur naturally in coastal PNW conifer understory and are commonly planted together as an evergreen native shrub layer (model placeholder, unverified).
relations.context: PNW coastal forest understory

relations.text: E-Flora BC places both Vaccinium ovatum and Gaultheria shallon in coastal lowland to montane forest of the Coastal Western Hemlock zone — the same habitat classes, so they co-occur naturally in the Vancouver region.
relations.context: derived: overlapping habitat classes on the two atlas pages (forest, lowland, montane, coastal; modal zone CWH); the source does not state the association itself
relations.note: habitat co-occurrence, not a planting-design recommendation; the model placeholder m1 says the same from general knowledge and is retired by this claim
relations.retired_reason: REL-R1 withdrawn 2026-11-02 (brief 'Verification Workbench' §03A, methods M43): a shared E-Flora habitat class is an indirect connection expressed through the habitat / bgc_zone concept nodes both plants link to, not a direct companion relation; record kept as history
relations.citation: In Klinkenberg, Brian. (Editor) 2020. E-Flora BC: Electronic Atlas of the Plants of British Columbia [eflora.bc.ca]. Lab for Advanced Spatial Analysis, Department of Geography, University of British Columbia, Vancouver. [Accessed: 2026-10-29]

relations.text: Once established, Gaultheria shallon can spread into and under Vaccinium ovatum; the huckleberry usually holds its own because it is taller, but smaller plantings can be overrun (model placeholder, unverified).
relations.context: designed plantings, shade
relations.note: most valuable relation to confirm with a practitioner. Sourced claims now establish the mechanism (suckering/rhizomatous, forms thickets — RHS, OSU, USDA) but no source states the effect on huckleberry specifically.

relations.text: Gaultheria shallon is often used as an evergreen groundcover beneath Acer palmatum; both accept filtered shade and acidic soil (model placeholder, unverified).
relations.context: designed gardens, PNW
relations.note: mechanism supported piecewise (MOBOT: maple as sun-dappled understory/woodland-margin tree; RHS/E-Flora: salal in shade; both on acidic soil) but no source describes the pairing — stays a placeholder

relations.text: Vaccinium ovatum can form the shrub layer under a small Acer palmatum canopy; the maple's shallow roots and the huckleberry's slow establishment both argue for planting the shrub first (model placeholder, unverified).
relations.context: designed gardens, PNW
relations.note: huckleberry's slow establishment now sourced (USDA slow; RHS 10–20 yr); shade tolerance sourced (GPP); the pairing itself is not — stays a placeholder

relations.text: E-Flora BC records both Arctostaphylos uva-ursi and Cornus nuttallii in the Coastal Western Hemlock zone at low elevation and in the same habitat class (forest), so they co-occur naturally in the Vancouver region.
relations.context: derived: shared habitat class (forest) and the CWH zone on the two atlas pages (minimum elevations 6 m and 0 m, province-wide means 1129 m and 194 m; modal zones IDF / CWH — a modal zone other than CWH/CDF means the plant is marginal in the coastal zone); the source does not state the association itself
relations.note: habitat co-occurrence, not a planting-design recommendation; two plants sharing a habitat class may still compete (see the salal placeholders)
relations.retired_reason: REL-R1 withdrawn 2026-11-02 (brief 'Verification Workbench' §03A, methods M43): a shared E-Flora habitat class is an indirect connection expressed through the habitat / bgc_zone concept nodes both plants link to, not a direct companion relation; record kept as history
relations.citation: In Klinkenberg, Brian. (Editor) 2020. E-Flora BC: Electronic Atlas of the Plants of British Columbia [eflora.bc.ca]. Lab for Advanced Spatial Analysis, Department of Geography, University of British Columbia, Vancouver. [Accessed: 2026-11-02]

The value's fall_colour=false cannot be confirmed from the cached text: the 'Colour & Scent' season table renders only as its headings, so the autumn foliage entry is unreadable. The page describes 'A neat, erect, evergreen shrub'.
vaccinium-ovatum:seasonal_interest:rhs01.missing_context: fall_colour=false is not readable in the cached seasonal table; it may be an inference from 'evergreen'.

vaccinium-ovatum:seasonal_interest:usdap.locator: CHARACTERISTICS > Flower Color, Bloom Period, Foliage Color, Fruit/Seed Color, Fruit/Seed Conspicuous, Fruit/Seed Period, Leaf Retention
vaccinium-ovatum:seasonal_interest:usdap.excerpt: Flower Color: White ... Fruit/Seed Color: Purple ... Fruit/Seed Conspicuous: Yes ... Leaf Retention: Yes ... Bloom Period: Late Spring
vaccinium-ovatum:seasonal_interest:usdap.explanation: USDA characteristics give Flower Color White, Bloom Period Late Spring, Foliage Color Green, Fruit/Seed Color Purple, Fruit/Seed Conspicuous Yes, Fruit/Seed Period Begin and End Summer, and Leaf Retention Yes, all matching the claim. Flowering months 5-6 is the claim's own mapping of 'Late Spring', as its note records; the source gives no months.
vaccinium-ovatum:seasonal_interest:usdap.missing_context: USDA also rates Flower Conspicuous: No, which the claim does not carry.

vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:eflor.locator: Habitat / Range; Ecology > Ecological Framework table (Elevation; Modal BEC Zone; All BEC Zones)
vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:eflor.excerpt: Dry to moist, open forests in the lowland and montane zones; frequent in SW BC, rare near Prince Rupert; S to S CA.
vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:eflor.explanation: E-Flora's Habitat/Range gives dry to moist open forests in the lowland and montane zones, frequent in SW BC; the Ecological Framework table gives elevation min 2, average 185, max 1650 m, modal BEC zone CWH, and zones CDF(3), CWH(102), ESSF(3), ICH(4), MH(2), SBS(1), all matching the claim's value. 'Coastal' is supported by the Indicator Plants text (hypermaritime to maritime, coastal locations only). The statement that Vancouver sits in the CWH zone is the claim's own context, not on the page.
vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:eflor.missing_context: The BEC table is derived from 118 BC Ministry field plots (data updated 2013); the 'Vancouver is in CWH' link is external to the source.

vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:usdaplants0.excerpt: Drought Tolerance: Medium ... Moisture Use: Low
vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:usdaplants0.explanation: USDA rates Drought Tolerance Medium and Moisture Use Low, which the claim text reports accurately. Recording a 'medium' rating as a drought resistance is borderline, as the claim's note already says; the source does not call the plant drought tolerant.
vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:usdaplants0.missing_context: The rating is 'Medium', not high; the claim's category drops the degree.

vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:inat0.locator: iNaturalist API count with the claim's filters (cache total_results)
vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:inat0.explanation: The cached live API query with the same filters (place 27530, taxon 48349, verifiable, CC0/CC-BY/CC-BY-NC) returns total_results 29, identical to the claim's 29 licensed verifiable observations; no drift since the 2026-10-30 pull, though small drift would be expected and acceptable for this kind of count. The research-grade (24), all-licence (33) and year-range figures were not re-fetched and are unverified here. The API confirms taxon 48349 is Vaccinium ovatum and place 27530 is Greater Vancouver, BC.
vaccinium-ovatum:vancouver_context:inat0.missing_context: The research_grade, all_licences and years sub-values were not re-checked; counts reflect observer effort as the claim's note says.

vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:gpp01.locator: Quick Facts > Sun/Light Exposure; Culture Notes
vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:gpp01.excerpt: Sun/Light Exposure: full sun to deep shade
vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:gpp01.explanation: GPP Quick Facts give 'full sun to deep shade', and Culture Notes add that it does equally well in deep shade but may not flower or fruit, which the claim text reports. The four-category expansion covers that range. The page describes an evergreen shrub ('Plant Type: shrub').

vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:osu01.explanation: OSU states 'Sun to part shade', matching the claim's Full sun and Part sun/part shade categories. The page describes a 'Broadleaf, evergreen shrub'.

vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:rhs01.excerpt: Position Full sun Partial shade Aspect East–facing or South–facing or West–facing Exposure Sheltered
vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:rhs01.explanation: RHS gives Position Full sun / Partial shade and Exposure Sheltered, matching the claim's three categories. The page describes 'A neat, erect, evergreen shrub'.
vaccinium-ovatum:exposure:rhs01.missing_context: RHS also restricts Aspect to east-, south- or west-facing (not north-facing), which the claim omits.

vaccinium-ovatum:growth_rate:usdaplants0.explanation: USDA characteristics state 'Growth Rate: Slow', matching the claim.

vaccinium-ovatum:habit:osu01.excerpt: neat, erect, compact generally, but can have erratic growth habit (e.g., some long erect shoots)
vaccinium-ovatum:habit:osu01.explanation: OSU describes the shrub as neat, erect and generally compact with occasional erratic growth such as long erect shoots; the claim text reproduces this and maps 'erect, compact' to Upright, a direct reading. The page describes a 'Broadleaf, evergreen shrub'. (GPP's Quick Facts independently give Growth Habit: upright.)

vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:osu01.locator: Description paragraph, parenthetical after the leaf description
vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:osu01.explanation: OSU's description notes, immediately after describing the glossy leaves, '(Used in the florist industry.)', which supports the cut-foliage use claimed. The page describes a 'Broadleaf, evergreen shrub'.
vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:osu01.missing_context: The source does not say which part is used; the placement implies foliage, as the claim reads it.

vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:rhs01.locator: How to Grow > Suggested planting locations and garden types
vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:rhs01.excerpt: City and courtyard gardens Cottage and informal garden Patio and container plants Edible fruit Flower borders and beds
vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:rhs01.explanation: RHS lists City and courtyard gardens, Cottage and informal garden, Patio and container plants, Edible fruit, and Flower borders and beds. Container planting and (via city/courtyard) small garden/space are well supported; 'edible fruit' to Urban agriculture is a loose mapping; the RHS entry is 'Flower borders and beds', not 'shrub borders' as the claim text states, so Mixed shrub border is a substitution. Cottage and informal garden is not represented.
vaccinium-ovatum:landscape_use:rhs01.missing_context: RHS's 'Flower borders and beds' and 'Cottage and informal garden' are not carried; 'shrub borders' in the claim text is not on the page.

vaccinium-ovatum:pest_susceptibility:rhs.excerpt: May be susceptible to vine weevil larvae damage ... honey fungus (rarely), Powdery mildews, root rot and chlorosis due to iron and manganese deficiency
vaccinium-ovatum:pest_susceptibility:rhs.explanation: RHS lists vine weevil larvae (especially container-grown) and birds under Pests, and honey fungus (rarely), powdery mildews, root rot and chlorosis from iron/manganese deficiency under Diseases. The claim's four categories map to vine weevil, powdery mildew, root rot and chlorosis; birds and honey fungus are noted as unmapped in the claim's note.
vaccinium-ovatum:pest_susceptibility:rhs.missing_context: Vine weevil risk is tied to container growing; chlorosis is tied to iron/manganese deficiency (i.e. wrong soil pH), conditions the category list drops.

vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:gpp01.excerpt: Once established it is drought tolerant, but flowering and fruiting is better with occasional watering during dry weather.
vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:gpp01.explanation: GPP states that once established the plant is drought tolerant, with the caveat that flowering and fruiting are better with occasional dry-weather watering. The claim carries the 'once established' condition in its context. The page describes a shrub.
vaccinium-ovatum:resistances:gpp01.missing_context: Drought tolerance is at the cost of flowering/fruiting unless watered occasionally in dry weather.

vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:gpp01.excerpt: Provide plants with a well-drained or sandy soil. If the drainage is adequate it will tolerate clay.
vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:gpp01.explanation: GPP's Culture Notes call for well-drained or sandy soil and say clay is tolerated if drainage is adequate, matching the claim text and the Well-drained category. The page describes a shrub.
vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:gpp01.missing_context: Sandy soil and conditional clay tolerance are in the text but have no category in the value.

vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:rhs01.locator: Growing Conditions > Soil Types, Moisture, pH; Cultivation
vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:rhs01.excerpt: Plant in a sheltered site in well-drained, moisture-retentive, acidic soil, (pH 4.5-5.5)
vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:rhs01.explanation: RHS lists Soil Types Loam and Sand, Moisture moist but well-drained, pH Acid, and the Cultivation text asks for well-drained, moisture-retentive acidic soil at pH 4.5-5.5, supporting both Acidic and Well-drained; loam/sand are noted as unmapped.
vaccinium-ovatum:soil_type:rhs01.missing_context: RHS gives a specific pH 4.5-5.5 and the alternative of ericaceous compost in containers, which the categories drop.

vaccinium-ovatum:texture:gpp01.excerpt: The small leaves of this shrub create a fine texture, but its slightly irregular growth habit keeps it interesting.
vaccinium-ovatum:texture:gpp01.explanation: GPP states that the small leaves create a fine texture, matching the claim; the same sentence calls the plant a shrub. For the human reviewer: the USDA characteristics on file rate Foliage Texture 'Coarse', a cross-source disagreement not flagged in the queue.

vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:g.locator: Quick Facts > Plant Height (10-year); Plant Width/Spread (10-year)
vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:g.excerpt: Plant Height (10-year): 6 ft. 0 in. (1.83 meters) Plant Width/Spread (10-year): 4 ft. 0 in. (1.22 meters)
vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:g.explanation: GPP Quick Facts give a 10-year height of 6 ft 0 in (1.83 m) and 10-year width of 4 ft 0 in (1.22 m), exactly the claim's values. The page describes an evergreen shrub.

vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:r.explanation: RHS gives Time to Maturity 10-20 years, matching the claim's 10-20 years. The page labels it time to maturity rather than 'time to ultimate height' as the claim's measure field says, a wording difference consistent with RHS's size convention.
vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:r.missing_context: UK growing conditions; the measure is RHS 'Time to Maturity'.

vaccinium-ovatum:time_to_intended_size:u.explanation: USDA characteristics give Height at 20 Years, Maximum 8 ft, which is 2.44 m, rounded by the claim to 2.4 m at 20 years.

vaccinium-ovatum:toxicity:usdaplants01.explanation: USDA characteristics state 'Toxicity: None', matching usda_rating 'none'. The claim deliberately keeps humans and pets 'unknown' because the USDA rating is a single conservation-planting characteristic; the source gives no human- or pet-specific statement, so that scoping is consistent with the page. The page also lists Palatable Human: Yes and Berry/Nut/Seed Product: Yes.
vaccinium-ovatum:toxicity:usdaplants01.missing_context: The USDA rating scale (None/Slight/Moderate/Severe) is aimed at livestock/conservation use, as the claim's note says.

rules.KG-R1: a KPU landscape-use label that names a design concept maps to it (ontology maps_to); a plant with a sourced claim on that use is derived suited to the concept, with the claim as evidence
rules.KG-R2: a quantitative height claim places the plant in every height band its range intersects; conditions, cultivar and place travel with the edge
rules.KG-R3: a vertical layer corresponds to the height bands its plants occupy (to confirm)
rules.KG-R5: a plant occupies a vertical layer when its growth form typically forms that layer and a height band the layer corresponds to is reached by one of its height claims; conditions travel with the edge
rules.KG-R4: requires_trait relations checked against the plant's live edges: met / unmet (single-valued facet with non-matching claims) / unknown (no claim); all required met → candidate, never promoted; any unmet → contradicted; else evidence missing
rules.M29: growth form read from the sources, never inferred from 'Broadleaf evergreen'
rules.M48: the XYZ projection: visible edges aggregate the live kg.json edges between the same pair; status is the strongest underlying status, verification is verified only if a live supporting claim is verified; unknown design links are listed as gaps, never drawn
rules.M49: the Explorer projection: species, attribute cells, five functions with requirements, exactly species × functions link cells, every relation record (retired = history), 45 pairs with shared concepts, direct records and complementarity hypotheses; status, verification and AI evidence check are three separate fields on every record; nothing is promoted, nothing unknown is drawn
